newsitem.title: USA: Environmentalists sue California over toxins.
newsitem.headline: Environmentalists sue California over toxins.

text.p: Environmental and labour groups sued California Gov. Pete Wilson on Wednesday for allegedly failing to warn residents about scores of toxins believed to cause birth defects, infertility and other disorders.

The groups, including the Natural Resources Defence Council, the AFL-CIO and United Farmworkers, sued Wilson, a Republican, and the California Environmental Protection Agency for allegedly failing to add to the state's list of reproductive toxins and carcinogens 66 chemicals commonly used to keep pests off food crops and out of homes.

Under California's Safe Drinking Water and Toxic Enforcement Act approved by voters in 1986, the state is required to publish a list of reproductive toxins and to update the list each year, according to the lawsuit, which was filed in Sacramento Superior Court.
The warnings help California workers and consumers avoid exposure to dangerous chemicals and encourage manufacturers to find safer alternatives, the Natural Resources Defence Council said.

Wilson's failure to add the 66 chemicals to the state's list of toxins violated the 1986 act because they were identified as toxins by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency 2-1/2 years ago, the lawsuit said.

"U.S. EPA found that these chemicals are known, or reasonably anticipated, to cause birth-defects, miscarriages, infertility, or other reproductive disorders," Gina Solomon, senior staff scientist for the Natural Resources Defence Council said.
"Pregnant women, children, and workers who are highly exposed have a right to know that these chemicals may pose risks to reproductive health so that they can choose to avoid unnecessary exposures."

The toxins are used by farmers on more than 75 food crops. The lawsuit asks the court to order the state to include the chemicals on its list of toxins. California's EPA said it was reviewing hundreds of compounds, and may list the chemicals cited in the lawsuit once the agency's review is completed.
